The story spans a period of roughly three and a half years, requiring significant compression of time to fit into a short-story format, which the author handles adeptly. Entire construction phases lasting months (such as "May through November" or "the second winter") are effectively summarized into single paragraphs that capture the repetitive, grinding nature of institutional delays and bureaucratic ineptitude. At the same time, the narrative slows down (stretches) at just the right moments to ground the story in specific, vivid scenes—such as the afternoon Tomás spends catching water in a trash can to save the archive, Dr. Amsel listening to the first autumn storm on the new roof, and the brief closing dialogue over the index card. This balance allows the reader to feel the prolonged exhaustion of the three-year ordeal without the pacing of the story itself becoming tedious.
